case_name: Bandula Bhavani, E.G.Dist vs Bandula Upparayya, W.G.Dist on 6 December, 2018

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Petitioner (wife or husband) — full case name

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Multiple parties filed petitions to withdraw original petitions and transfer them to different courts based on various grounds such as distance, threat to life, difficulty in travelling, etc.

legal_principles.principle: Access to justice is a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution.
legal_principles.held: A person's access to justice is a guaranteed fundamental right under the Constitution and particularly Article 21.
cited_cases: Brij Mohan Lal v. Union of India and Ors, (2012) 6 SCC 502

legal_principles.principle: Unduly long delay in disposal of cases can lead to blatant violation of the Rule of law and adverse impact on access to justice.
legal_principles.held: Unduly long delay has the effect of bringing about blatant violation of the Rule of law and adverse impact on the common man's access to justice.

legal_principles.principle: Access to justice includes qualitative access, ensuring just and inequitable judicial outcomes.
legal_principles.held: Access to justice is, therefore, much more than improving an individual's access to courts, or guaranteeing representation. It must be defined in terms of ensuring that legal and judicial outcomes are just and inequitable
cited_cases: United Nations Development Programme, Access to Justice-Practice Note (2004)

legal_principles.principle: The right of access to an independent judiciary is vital for the Rule of law.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that the stay of investigation or trial for significant periods of time runs counter to the principle of Rule of law, wherein the rights and aspirations of citizens are intertwined with expeditious conclusion of matters.
cited_cases: Brij Mohan Lal v. Union of India and Ors, (2012) 6 SCC 502
